newsitem.title: UK: Pearson declines comment on Lazards talk.
newsitem.headline: Pearson declines comment on Lazards talk.

text.p: Britain's Pearson Plc declined comment on Monday on speculation that the company may sell its Lazard merchant banking interests.
Pearson has a 50 percent stake in London's Lazard Brothers plus smaller stakes in Lazard Freres in Paris and New York.

There has been speculation that new Pearson chief executive Marjorie Scardino may decide to sell the stakes as they do not fit into the company's core Information, Education and Entertainment divisions.

Fuel was added to the fire by a weekend interview with Michel David-Weill, senior partner with Lazard Freres and a Pearson director, who said that Lazard might sell its 48 million Pearson shares if the company withdraws from banking.
The Lazard group owns some 48 million Pearson shares -- a stake of over eight percent -- through a Paris-based investment company.
David-Weill told the Pearson-owned Financial Times at the weekend that the Pearson stake could be sold but "not to a party which could be hostile".
Pearson shares have firmed in recent days on hopes that Scardino will focus the company's activities more sharply. They added 11.5p to 760p by 1050 GMT on Monday.
